result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: EmbedController#best calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: embed_url) with only the referer check (spoofable) and no rate limit, while TopicRetriever's throttle uses key "retrieved:#{@embed_url}" (per-URL setnx with 60s expiry), so varying the query string yields distinct keys and no global throttle on enqueue. Unbounded unauthenticated job enqueueing and Redis keys, plus outbound fetches to arbitrary embeddable-host URLs, is a plausible DoS/abuse defect introduced by this code.

judged_text: The controller enqueues a retrieve_topic Sidekiq job for any user-supplied embed_url before any host validation or throttling runs (validation happens later inside the job via TopicRetriever), and TopicRetriever's throttle key is the full embed_url string, so varying the query string bypasses it entirely. Unauthenticated attackers (the Referer gate is satisfied by a spoofed header) flood the Sidekiq queue with arbitrary-length job payloads, create unbounded Redis keys via the per-URL setnx throttle, and trigger unbounded outbound fetches — a cheap queue/Redis exhaustion and fetch-amplification DoS against the forum.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no existing `TopicEmbed` is found it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` based solely on `params.require(:embed_url)`; the only pre-filter (`ensure_embeddable`) validates the *Referer* host, not the supplied `embed_url`. The actual `embed_url` host validation and throttling occur later in `TopicRetriever#retrieve`. The throttle key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` (full URL string), so attackers can bypass throttling by varying query strings/fragments and force many distinct Redis keys plus repeated fetches via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(... open(url) ...)`. Because referer is header-controlled and `current_user` can be nil, this enables unauthenticated queue/Redis growth and outbound fetch amplification (at least to the configured `embeddable_host`).
